title: Anyone know the coherence length of this laser?

posts.topic_title: Anyone know the coherence length of this laser?
posts.author: MichaelH
posts.post_subject: Anyone know the coherence length of this laser?
posts.content_md:
Yes, I know I theoretically can measure it but there are two problems...

1) I have a commission I'm working on and can't afford to strip my table and set up an interferometer.

2) (I was going to say that my table might not be large enough since the CL appears to be > 1' but since I'm not testing stability I could set up a small interferometer and as long as the CL isn't > 10' I'd be ok. So, see #1)

I have a Melles Griot 05-LHP-791 that's putting out about 12mW and I just discovered that one of the beams in my copy setup was ~10" longer than the other. I've been getting reasonably bright holograms but still thought this finding was alarming. I reset the legs and shot a test and for the life of me I can't tell the difference between a hologram with 62/72" legs and the one with 62/62" legs as far as brightness goes.

So either the CL of this laser is at least a foot (or likely two feet) or I've discovered some heretofore unknown magic. I think the former much more likely. 

Anyone happen to know for sure? A Googling didn't turn up any answers for me.

If I understand well you got an interferometric region (supposing that the laser operates at few longitudinal modes) that is a multiple of 2L (L=cavity length), with this path length the temporal coherence can interfere with itself. Your laser coherence is defined as the path length difference for which fringe visibility in a Michelson interferometer is reduced to 1/e^2 points.

posts.post_subject: Anyone know the coherence length of this laser?
posts.content_md:
I'll say up front I don't have an answer to your question...

I have a similar laser (bought from Sam), 11mW, 17" long. It has so much conherence length that I almost stopped worrying about it entirely until I got caught by it the other night.

I was set up to make some H1s. I usually direct the object beam from one side, and add another mirror on the opposite side to redirect some light back onto the object. This usually works fine, even though the light from the 'far' side has 6-8 inches extra path length.

When the H1 came out, it looked like it was lit entirely from the 'far' side - nothing at all on the 'near' side.

Turns out the object beam length was wayyy short. When I corrected it, the object lighting was evenly balanced.

My non-specific experience is that these mid-power Henes have gobs of coherence length - better than 12" I think.

As a side question, what happens when you exceed the coherence length? In this case, I just lost image brightness. But in the past when using diode lasers, I seem to rememeber that things got out of focus. Anyone care to comment?

posts.content_md:
[quote:53cb740af4="MichaelH"]Yes, I know I theoretically can measure it but there are two problems...

1) I have a commission I'm working on and can't afford to strip my table and set up an interferometer.

[/quote:53cb740af4]

You say you can't afford to strip the table down. Is this necessary? Can you insert a mirror at some raw beam part of the setup, before the beamsplitter, say, to bleed some of the beam off. If space is the consideration and you have two beamsplitters, ie two more than the one you're using, can you use an "inline" Michaelson:

====beam====\(bs_1))=====|(bs_2)=====|(mirror)

The light goes through bs_1 (some of it is divertied "down", but we'll ignore that) and continues on to bs_2. From bs_2 some is reflected to bs_1 and goes "up" while some is transmitted through to the mirror. From the mirror it reflects back through bs_2 to bs_1 and also reflectes "up". The path difference is, of course, the distance between bs_2 and the mirror. You may want to slightly tilt bs_2 so as not to get ringing between bbs_2 and the mirror. This setup just needs an unused edge of the table so if the bled beam can be run along an edge of the table you can set up the "inline" Michaelson.

If you need the odd beamsplitter, let me know and I can ship overnight.
